newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Liechtenstein to form new government April 9.
newsitem.headline: Liechtenstein to form new government April 9.

text.p: Liechtenstein's parliament will name a new government on April 9 following the decision of one of the parties to leave the ruling coalition, head of the ruling Fatherland Union (VU) party Oswald Kranz said on Tuesday.

The Progressive Citizens Party Liechtenstein (FBPL) voted on Monday to split with the VU, ending what is thought to be Europe's longest-serving ruling coalition, set up in 1938, the same year Nazi Germany annexed Austria, which borders Liechtenstein.
Mountainous Liechtenstein, covering an area of only 160 square kilometres (62 square miles) is also bordered by Switzerland.
The Principality's parliament will select the five-member government, which will be formally nominated by Prince Hans Adam, the hereditary ruler.

The decision to end the coalition followed general elections on February 2, when the FBPL lost a parliamentary seat to the pro-ecology Free List party, leaving the FBLU only 10 seats in Liechtenstein's 25-member parliament . The VU retained its 13 parliamentary seats.
The latest changes will allow the FBPL to create its own party identity, a new challenge in a country where the two main parties had been virtually interchangeable.
"The work in government will be more efficient, but at the same time the political climate could become more heated," Kranz told Reuters.
